0.9.0 is a security release. It closes the findings of an audit of what a scanned tree can make rust-doctor run, write or print: a scan with Clippy off now starts no program the tree selects, no write follows a symlink the tree commits, and the report no longer leaks the tail of a quoted path or a one-line private key. One change breaks a workflow: the Action stops posting the pull request comment from the job that builds the pull request. Read [Breaking changes](#breaking-changes) before upgrading a workflow that comments.

## Breaking changes

### The Action no longer posts the pull request comment

`uses: arthjean/rust-doctor@v0` builds the pull request's code, build scripts and procedural macros included, so it should never share a job with a token that writes to the pull request. Its `comment` and `comment-on-clean` inputs are removed, and so is the step that posted the sticky comment. The Action now uploads `report.json`, `summary.md` and the `clean` flag in the `rust-doctor-report` artifact, and a new action, `arthjean/rust-doctor/comment@v0`, posts the comment from a second job that checks nothing out, installs nothing and reads only that artifact ([c33592c](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/c33592c)).

A workflow that keeps the old layout still scans and gates, but no comment is posted, and GitHub only warns about the unknown inputs.

**Upgrade path.** Grant the scan job `contents: read` alone and post the comment from a job of its own:

```yaml
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  scan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: arthjean/rust-doctor@v0

  comment:
    needs: scan
    if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      - uses: arthjean/rust-doctor/comment@v0
        # with:
        #   comment-on-clean: false
```

`comment: false` becomes leaving the `comment` job out, and `comment-on-clean` moves, unchanged, to `arthjean/rust-doctor/comment`. A workflow written by `rust-doctor ci install --comment` takes the same layout with `rust-doctor ci install --comment --update`. Every `rust-cache` step the Action and the generated workflow run now saves from the default branch only and never caches `~/.cargo/bin`.

## Security

A scan with every Clippy rule off was documented as compiling nothing. It still started programs the tree chose, through git and through Cargo. Each path is now closed and a fixture proves it, one marker per program, across the eight scopes, `rules explain` and `ci install --dry-run` ([daaa230](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/daaa230)).

- **git.** Every git call blanks the clean, smudge and process commands of each filter driver the configuration names, includes resolved and LFS included, and fails closed on a git that ignores the override. It also disables hooks, so a snapshot's index write no longer starts `post-index-change`, and refuses to bind to a git directory the tree commits as plain files ([0894068](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/0894068)).
- **Cargo and rustup.** A Clippy-off scan no longer probes the cargo, clippy and rustc versions, which ran a workspace `[alias] clippy` or a `rust-toolchain.toml` path toolchain; the report publishes the three as `null`, meaning "not probed". `cargo metadata` runs under `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN` set to a toolchain name ([0ca4828](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/0ca4828)). `rules explain` and `ci install` find the workspace root from the manifests instead of `cargo metadata` ([90bbe00](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/90bbe00)).
- **Writes through planted links.** A committed `target/` could link the baseline, staged or cache directory, or a probe or staging file, and the next baseline or staged scan truncated its destination. Those writes now refuse a linked component and fall back to a private target or skip the store; a `.cargo-husky/hooks` link out of the tree receives nothing either ([310ec2d](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/310ec2d)).
- **Baseline snapshots.** A snapshot was created under a world-writable `/tmp`, where another user could plant a `.cargo/config.toml` or `rust-toolchain.toml` Cargo would walk up to. Its parent is now the first of the temporary directory, `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` and the cache home that no other user can write along its whole path; with none, the scan reports `baseline-temp-unavailable` ([7d4bd08](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/7d4bd08)).
- **Installers.** `setup`, `hook install git` and `ci install` confined their writes to the toplevel git reported, which a tree's own configuration can move. They now require the nearest `.git` on disk to be that toplevel, and exit non-zero naming both paths otherwise ([13d82a8](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/13d82a8)). Every repository-derived name or command line the installers print is sanitized of terminal control characters ([8ae84b0](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/8ae84b0)).
- **Advisory database.** Discovery accepts only a clone whose every remote is `https://github.com/rustsec/advisory-db`, read without starting git, so a `deny.toml` naming another database can no longer decide the `vulnerable_dependency` verdicts. A machine holding only another database reports `advisory-db-missing`; `--advisory-db` still reads any database you name ([d278791](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/d278791)).
- **Report redaction.** A path opened by a backtick or a double quote now ends at its match, so a space or an apostrophe inside it no longer cuts it short and leaks the rest; `C:\Users\First Last\...`, verbatim and UNC roots are externalized whole, and the home falls back to `USERPROFILE` when `HOME` is unset ([3c5060f](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/3c5060f)). A private key written on its header's line, as an escaped one-line key is, is masked to its footer, in the report error and in the Cargo stderr excerpt ([71ce7a1](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/71ce7a1)).
- **`why --report`.** The suppression directive it prints pasted the saved report's code verbatim, so a crafted report could hand you Rust to compile. It now prints a directive only for a well-formed lint path ([ecd4b9e](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/ecd4b9e)).
- **npm launcher.** The launcher found its native package through Node's resolver, which climbs every ancestor `node_modules`, so a same-named package the install never placed could run. It now reads only the wrapper's own `node_modules` and its sibling, which covers the nested, npm, bun and pnpm layouts ([1aa368d](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/1aa368d)).

## Changed behavior

- A Clippy-off scan of a workspace that only resolves to a path toolchain is refused with exit 2 instead of running that toolchain. Without rustup, `cargo metadata` runs unpinned as before ([0ca4828](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/0ca4828)).
- The installers' fallback to `.` is gone: a workspace whose `.git` does not sit at git's reported toplevel makes `setup`, `hook install git` and `ci install` fail. A linked worktree and a submodule install as before ([13d82a8](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/13d82a8)).

## Agent hook

`hook install claude|cursor` and `hook run` take `--no-clippy`, which turns every Clippy rule off whatever `rust-doctor.toml` says, so the end-of-turn hook compiles nothing. An agent hook installed without it, directly or through `setup`, now states that it runs `cargo clippy` and the tree's build code at the end of every turn with your authority, and `why --help` and `hook run --help` carry the same warning ([4f88f2b](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/4f88f2b)).

## Internal

The release workflow pins every third-party action to a commit and installs npm 11.21.1 and Node 22.13.0 exactly ([af37ab1](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/af37ab1)), verifies the crate in a job that holds no OIDC permission, and restores no cache, so every shipped build starts cold ([f941337](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/f941337)). The remaining commits are the audit remediation tracker and its certifications.

## Install

```bash
npx rust-doctor@latest
```

```bash
cargo install rust-doctor
```
